rules.statement: A tenant configured to fail closed on lag (`cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.tenants`) is not decided on when the oldest document its evaluation reads was last confirmed by the store longer ago than `fail-closed.max-lag`: the request is indeterminate (503) unless a DENY matches. Other tenants, and views within the bound, are decided as usual.
guards: runtime:DocumentSnapshotViewsTest#a fail-closed tenant past its lag bound is unresolved, others decide

rules.source: RFC 0003 §4.4 F9, F10; RC1-50; review L1 of #1200; #1215; review L4 of #1231
rules.statement: The periodic revalidation cannot be turned off or left unbounded: `cosec.authorization.snapshot.revalidate-interval` is at least 1 second, at most 5 minutes, less than `lag-warn` and, with fail-closed tenants, less than `fail-closed.max-lag`, or startup fails naming it. Installed documents are revalidated by periodic passes, each a conditional read of the store per document, never a local copy, and a reset of the change channel reloads them all. A pass starts every interval or, when the previous one is still in flight, as soon as it ends; a change whose invalidation was lost, or whose reload failed, is installed by the first pass that reaches its document after the change is readable. A pass that has finished no document for `storeReadTimeout` and has no read in flight is abandoned at the next tick; a pass with a read in flight never is. A pass does not wait for a load of a document that has been in flight longer than `storeReadTimeout`: the load confirms its document when it ends.

rules.statement: An entry for a document the store does not hold never evicts one it holds: such entries have a bound of their own (`maxAbsent` per family) and evict only each other, so however many ids without a document a client names, every document a family holds within its bound stays installed.
guards: runtime:DocumentSnapshotSourceTest#a flood of ids without a document never evicts a document

rules.statement: A revision whose compilation fails, with an exception or a VirtualMachineError such as a StackOverflowError, is installed as failed: the source never keeps serving the revision before it in its place.

rules.statement: Every key a deployment writes to Redis lives under its one `cosec.key-prefix`: snapshot documents, control-plane records, candidates, shadow reports, revocations, memberships, API keys, rate limit counters and OAuth states. Two deployments on one Redis that differ in it share no key. An environment that sets one of the three prefixes it replaced fails startup as a key CoSec does not read, and no property turns that check off, so no revocation is left where nothing reads it.

rules.statement: A staged platform candidate is compiled for the shadow comparison only: what an instance enforces compiles with the limits and attributes of the platform document it installed, so staging a change, or withdrawing it, neither fails an enforced document closed nor brings one back. rules.statement: A stored document that does not compile on an instance is reported as such: a request that needs it is Indeterminate with Cause.DocumentInvalid at the stored revision, never SourceUnavailable, which says the store could not be read; the client's 503 is the same as for any unavailability, with nothing of the compiler's message; the instance logs it once per revision, digest and inputs it compiled against, and once more when a revision compiles; and its health names the document and revision as invalid.

rules.statement: A snapshot document's header is read from its body: the stored bytes are the whole document, and the only way to make a SnapshotDocument is SnapshotDocuments, which reads schema, revision and publishedAt from them (read) or from the document it encodes (of). No main code of any module calls the constructor, so no store, candidate or test kit can state a revision its bytes contradict, and the revision an instance reports installed is the revision of the content it enforces. A shadow candidate's record holds its window, its base revision and its document only; a record that states the header beside the document is refused as an unreadable candidate.

rules.source: RFC 0003 §4.4 (the future of a maintenance call)
rules.statement: The future of `revalidate` or `recompile` completes only after, for every document it covers, a load that started after the call: `revalidate` covers every document installed at the call, `recompile` every app and tenant document idle or loading at the call. A load already in flight at the call, which may have read or compiled before it, is followed by another, and the future waits for that one.

rules.source: RFC 0013 B2b (the family bound under a burst)
rules.statement: A family holds at most its bound plus the smaller of its bound and 4,096 entries of each kind (documents; entries for documents the store does not hold), plus the entries being installed or loaded at that moment; an install that finds its kind over that evicts on the installing thread before it answers its waiters. Evictions never take a kind below its bound, and passes running at once leave a kind at its bound when every victim was idle: they never stop above it.

runtime:SnapshotFamilyBoundTest#installs within the cap leave eviction to housekeeping, which takes the family back to its bound

rules.statement: What a spent drain budget leaves is not left waiting on the compile queue. An event the source's own work produces (a read's answer, failure or timeout, a compilation's result, an effect's failure, a retry coming due) is taken by the thread that holds the key's flag or the next one to take it, before any budget check and uncounted. A caller event left by a spent budget is handed to the source's own threads, where it waits for at most the compilation a pool thread is running; when the pool refuses it housekeeping runs it, and when that refuses too, its offerer does.

rules.statement: An effect that throws ends its key's load in flight as a transient failure and the key goes on: a step offers at most one `EffectFailed`, and an `EffectFailed`'s own step offers none, so no thread loops on a key whose effects keep failing.

rules.statement: A request's cold load timeout runs from the call: its load or its timer answers it within `coldLoadTimeout` of `request()`. The request is registered before its offer, so `close` answers it whatever the drain does; its timer is armed when the offer returns, with what is left of the bound, and only if it is not yet answered; an offer that throws leaves it answered and untimed.

rules.source: roadmap §9 (the data plane's Redis credential read-only); CoCache 8.1.0 read-only stores
rules.statement: A process that does not run the control plane reads the snapshot documents and the candidates read-only, so a Redis user with read permission on them is enough and Redis refuses it a write; a process that runs the control plane writes them. Which one a process is follows the condition the control plane is wired on and nothing else: a cocache.* property or customizer that changes it, either way, fails the creation of the store.
